whats_this.heading: Welcome to Adoptive Parent Guide
whats_this.description: You're sponsoring or being sponsored by an adoptive parent. Adoption cases require additional documentation because USCIS must confirm that the adoptive parent-child relationship meets U.S. immigration law.
quick_instructions: Review Pakistan guardianship nuances vs. U.S. adoption.
Verify the 2-year custody and residence rules.
Check required court and secondary evidence documents.
whats_this.disclaimer: Providing these documents does not automatically guarantee approval. USCIS will review your case to determine whether the adoptive parent-child relationship qualifies under U.S. immigration law.

tips: In Pakistan, guardianship orders alone do not automatically count as adoptions. You must satisfy U.S. immigration law standards.
Ensure the adoption was finalized before the child turned 16.
pitfalls: Failing to meet the strict 2-year legal custody and 2-year co-residence requirements before petition filing.

tips: If a new birth certificate listing the adoptive parents is unavailable, submit the original birth certificate together with court documents.
Provide clear evidence showing that the child lived with the parent for at least 2 years.
pitfalls: Submitting incomplete guardianship orders that do not grant full legal custody.

tips: Translations must be certified by a third-party translator. Self-translation is not permitted by USCIS.
pitfalls: Self-translating documents or submitting translation statements without translator credentials.

tips: Double-check that names are spelled consistently across all court decrees, birth certificates, and forms.
pitfalls: Submitting low-quality, blurry, or cut-off scans of legal court orders.
